Nor can half (ii) abort the block before half (i) runs: pre-fix, awaiting groupsApi.members with the spy resolving 200 plus the envelope succeeds and all four of half (ii)'s assertions hold, so nothing throws ahead of half (i). The design lists (i) first regardless.

mutant_substitution.legitimacy: ACCEPTED. WF-03_issue_resolving.md:104-117 scopes the clause to 'when the pre-fix failure is the code under test does not exist', on the ground that a pre-fix failure carrying no information about whether the test discriminates correct from wrong cannot satisfy fail-first -- 'a suite can fail against a missing module and still be vacuous against a broken one.' A type-only change is the same situation a fortiori: there is no pre-fix failure AT ALL at runtime, not merely an uninformative one. So the design is not stretching the rule to escape it, it is applying the rule where its own rationale bites harder. The structural premise is one I verified independently at the first gate: web/src/api/client.ts:158-169 ends in `return response.json() as Promise<T>`, a verbatim pass-through, and `as Promise<T>` is erased at emit -- so client.get<User[]> and client.get<GroupMemberPage> are byte-identical at runtime on the same spy body. Section 7.1's claim that no runtime row can carry decision (b)'s fail-first evidence is correct, and saying so plainly is better design than manufacturing a row that appears to.
mutant_substitution.discrimination_both_directions: ACCEPTED. The trap is the decoupling of the wire shape from its consumer, and the fix has two coupled halves: the retype of groupsApi.members (api side) and the six GroupsPage.tsx consumer edits (page side). M-1a breaks the page side while keeping the retype -- tsc must then reject the restored array-shaped reads, since `members ?? []` is GroupMemberPage | never[] and neither .map nor .length exists on it. M-1b breaks the api side while keeping the page edits -- tsc must then reject membersPage?.items over User[]. Each mutant fires on exactly one half, so together they show the probe tracks the coupling itself rather than merely breaking something. That is the discrimination WF-03's 'must target the specific traps the fix exists to handle' asks for.
mutant_substitution.npm_test_still_passes_under_m1a: ACCEPTED, and it is the sharpest part of the argument. Verified independently: under M-1a the new test file exercises groupsApi only -- groupsApi.members still returns the envelope and still hits /identity -- so rows 1-11 all pass; vitest transpiles via esbuild without type-checking, so GroupsPage's tsc errors cannot fail npm test; and no GroupsPage component test exists to import the mutated file. The expectation is therefore correct as stated. More importantly the REASONING is sound: a green npm test under M-1a is a measurement that the runtime suite is blind to the retype, which converts 'we chose not to write a render test' from an unevidenced omission into a demonstrated claim about where the detector actually lives. I accept it.
mutant_substitution.specified_precisely_enough_for_step_4b: YES, subject to N-1. Both mutants name the exact files and edits to revert (section 3.1's retype; section 3.2's six GroupsPage.tsx edits), the exact probe command (cd web && npm run type-check), the expected direction of failure, and the expected still-green command for M-1a. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR can apply either without a further decision.
mutant_substitution.not_applied_here: I did NOT apply either mutant. Applying at least one is TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's obligation at Step 4b (WF-03:118-121), and this step is bound to modify no file outside handoffs/. What I am passing is the SPECIFICATION of the mutants, not a measured outcome -- Step 4b still owes the measurement, and accepting its reported counts without applying one would be copying a claim.

revert_and_verify.detail: Section 7.1's third bullet states 'Revert discipline is binding (WF-03 Step 4's mutant rule)' and gives both sanctioned techniques -- a throwaway git worktree of the branch, or in place followed by git checkout -- <path> -- then requires, before the handoff completes, quoting (a) git status --porcelain web/ empty and (b) npm run type-check AND npm test green against the restored tree. The path substitution to web/ is correct, since M-1a/M-1b touch only web/, and requiring type-check green in addition to the suite is STRICTER than the workflow's floor, not looser.

fold_in_decision_c_note.detail: Section 4 rationale 1 now carries: 'that comment's own stated premise -- no existing Letflow caller depends on the array shape either way -- is stale today, because GroupsPage.tsx:76 passes [userId]. Decision (c) does not contradict the comment; it makes the comment's premise true again by removing the one caller that had drifted from it.' Both halves check out. GroupsPage.tsx:76 does pass [userId] to groupsApi.addMembers today, and groupsApi.addMembers is the only client call that sends the user_ids array shape at all -- so after decision (c) sends { user_id: userId }, no caller depends on the array shape and the comment's premise holds again. 'Restores rather than contradicts' is the accurate characterisation, and it is the right way to record it: it removes the apparent tension between decision (c) and core-directives' 'don't silently re-decide what a decision record already settled' instead of leaving a later reader to rediscover it.

issues.title: M-1a's predicted tsc error-site list should be read as a floor, not an exact-match assertion
issues.detail: M-1a expects tsc to error at the reverted GroupsPage.tsx :103, :223, :227 and :228, explained as '.map/.length do not exist on GroupMemberPage, and user_id does not exist on GroupMember'. The first three are certain: `members ?? []` is GroupMemberPage | never[], so .map at :103 and :227 and .length at :223 each raise TS2339. The :228 prediction is weaker. :228 is `user.id ?? user.user_id ?? ''` inside the callback of the :227 .map that has itself just failed to resolve -- when the callee errors, tsc types the call as any and the callback parameter as implicit any, so the diagnostic characteristically surfaces AT :227 (TS7006) rather than as a distinct :228 error, and the 'user_id does not exist on GroupMember' reasoning is unreachable because the element type is never computed. This is not a flaw in the mutant -- three certain errors on the page side under M-1a, and a certain error on the api side under M-1b, are more than enough to discriminate -- but a pre-committed exact site list invites a spurious mismatch at Step 4b, or worse, an attempt to adjust the mutant until a :228 diagnostic appears. The design already says the expected output is to be 'quoted verbatim in the test spec', i.e. from a real run, so this is self-correcting if the floor is understood.
issues.required_change: None to the design; PASS is not contingent on it. Binding forward instruction for Step 4/4b, which ORCH must carry into the TEST-DESIGNER and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR handoffs: treat M-1a's expectation as 'tsc errors on GroupsPage.tsx at the reverted members-consumer sites, including at least :103, :223 and :227', record verbatim whatever tsc actually emits, and do NOT modify the mutant to manufacture a diagnostic at :228. A site set that differs from the design's prediction while still showing type-check red under M-1a and green after the revert satisfies the probe.
